speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where you feel pain in your wrist, when the fever started, and what the skin lesions look like. To help me assess the severity, could you also tell me if you have had any recent insect bites or travel?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection.

The history of a preceding migratory polyarthritis (left knee), followed by septic arthritis of the wrist and fever, combined with recent sexual activity, is classic for this condition. I will not request further images or tests at this time as the clinical presentation is highly specific; please proceed with immediate blood cultures and empiric antibiotic therapy for Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
